This should be in html-aam instead.

I'm not sure the requirements here are what we want, though. I had expected the `img alt` to be used as the accessible name for the `video` element (and not go away when the poster is no longer showing). Having it as a child means users need to navigate to it, I think, which is a discoverability problem and might interfere with what users expect wrt navigating to the video controls.

body:
Thanks. That's a great pointer about html-aam. 

I appreciate the pushback on this part. Worth discussing. I had gathered feedback from some folks on the accessibility expectations for exposing poster alt that led to this proposed approach. A few points drove the idea of accessibly exposing poster independently of the video element here:

1. The spirit of the proposal was to offer an accessible description of the poster image itself (which it currently lacks). alt text that helpfully describes a poster image may frequently be a poor description of an entire video. One example: in practice, poster images are often used as a cover slide for a video, with text burned into its pixels and content that may not even appear in the video at all (youtube videos often have large text paired with surprised-looking people 😮 ). But even in cases where the poster uses a frame from somewhere in the video, that frame's visual description will likely differ from a description of the video itself.
2. The video element is not required to have an accessible name. When it's interactive it has internal accessibility affordances for its interactive controls, and it can have captions, etc. A poster could be considered a similar interface element to these.
3. The poster is conditionally displayed. Sometimes it's never displayed, if the video has autoplay for example. Other times it's hidden while the video is playing. Pairing its accessible description with its presence seemed reasonable.

Beyond these, it seemed there could be simplicity in allowing poster to build on img's accessibility, though I did wonder if UA's might be encouraged to prefix the description with something contextual like "video poster image: ...". Thanks!
